IHrmTimeTrackTimelog.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timelogs table for scalar fields (id, date, duration_seconds, billable, notes, created_at, updated_at). Relations exposed as ISummary objects: project via JOIN on hrm_time_track_project_id, task via LEFT JOIN on hrm_time_track_task_id (nullable), employee via JOIN on hrm_time_track_employee_id. Computed field timesheet_status from hrm_time_track_timesheets join (nullable). Soft-deleted records filtered at query level. Organization context from JWT authentication.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the timer session.

This UUID identifies the specific timer session and is used to reference it in subsequent operations such as updating or stopping the timer.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timers.id. Primary key uniquely identifying the timer session.

started_at.description:
Timestamp marking when the timer session began.

This field is set automatically when the timer is started and serves as the reference point for calculating elapsed time. The duration is calculated by subtracting started_at from the current time when the timer is stopped, rounded to the nearest minute for the resulting timelog.
started_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timers.started_at. Timestamp when the timer session began, set automatically when timer is created.

description.description:
Optional description of the work being performed during this timer session.

Employees can use this field to note what specific work is being done, providing context for the time being tracked. This description can be edited while the timer is running, allowing corrections and updates to work context without stopping the timer session.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timers.description. Nullable field for optional work notes describing what is being tracked.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this timer session is currently active.

This field distinguishes between active timers (is_active = true) and inactive timers (is_active = false). The system enforces that each employee can have at most one active timer at any time through a unique constraint on (hrm_time_track_employee_id, is_active).
is_active.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timers.is_active. Boolean flag indicating whether this timer session is currently running.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this timer record was created in the database.

This field is automatically set when the timer session is started and provides an audit trail of when the timer was initiated. It should match or be very close to the started_at timestamp.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timers.created_at. Timestamp when this timer record was created in the database.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this timer record was last modified.

This field is updated whenever the timer's description, project, or task assignment is edited while the timer is running. It provides visibility into when changes were made to the timer session context.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timers.updated_at. Timestamp when this timer record was last modified.

employee.description:
The employee who owns this timer session.

This nested object provides the employee's identifying information including their user identity (name, email), position, department, role, employment type, and status within the organization. The employee must be assigned to the project associated with this timer.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Relation mapping via JOIN on hrm_time_track_employee_id to hrm_time_track_employees table. Returns IHrmTimeTrackEmployee.ISummary with employee identity and organizational context.

project.description:
The project this timer is tracking time against.

This nested object provides the project's identifying information including name, description, color code, lifecycle status, budget hours, and planned dates. Project association is required when starting a timer, and the employee must be assigned to this project through hrm_time_track_project_members.
project.x-autobe-specification: Relation mapping via JOIN on hrm_time_track_project_id to hrm_time_track_projects table. Returns IHrmTimeTrackProject.ISummary with project identification and status information.

task.description:
The optional task within the project this timer is tracking.

This nested object (or null) provides the task's identifying information including title, priority, status, and relationships. Task association is optional when starting a timer. If specified, the task must belong to the project referenced in this timer, and the employee should have access to this task.
task.x-autobe-specification: Relation mapping via LEFT JOIN on hrm_time_track_task_id to hrm_time_track_tasks table. Returns IHrmTimeTrackTask.ISummary or null. Task association is optional when starting a timer.

IHrmTimeTrackTimer.description:
Complete timer session entity representing an active or completed time tracking session.

The timer captures the start timestamp, optional work description, and active status. It is associated with an employee (owner), a required project, and optionally a task within that project. The timer continues running until explicitly stopped (creating a timelog) or discarded (no timelog created).

Nested relationships provide complete context about the work being tracked: employee information shows who is tracking time, project details identify the work container, and task assignment (if present) specifies the granular work item. Timestamps indicate when the timer was started and last modified.
IHrmTimeTrackTimer.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timers table for scalar fields: id, started_at, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at. Relations exposed as nested objects: employee via JOIN on hrm_time_track_employee_id to hrm_time_track_employees (returns IHrmTimeTrackEmployee.ISummary), project via JOIN on hrm_time_track_project_id to hrm_time_track_projects (returns IHrmTimeTrackProject.ISummary), task via LEFT JOIN on hrm_time_track_task_id to hrm_time_track_tasks (returns IHrmTimeTrackTask.ISummary or null). FK columns (hrm_time_track_employee_id, hrm_time_track_project_id, hrm_time_track_task_id) are not exposed directly as they are represented by their corresponding object relations. The snapshots relation (has-many) is excluded as it's a composition accessed through a separate endpoint.

activeTasks.description:
List of active tasks assigned to the employee, including open and in-progress tasks.

Tasks are ordered by priority (highest first) and creation date (earliest first) to help the employee focus on urgent work. Only tasks with status 'open' or 'in-progress' are included. Completed, cancelled, or deleted tasks are excluded.

The list may be empty if the employee has no active tasks assigned.
activeTasks.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_track_tasks via JOIN on authenticated employee.id. Filter: status IN ('open', 'in-progress'), deleted_at IS NULL. Order by priority DESC, created_at ASC. Returns array of IHrmTimeTrackTask.ISummary objects. Empty array if no active tasks exist.

currentTimesheet.description:
The timesheet for the current week (Monday-Sunday), or null if no timesheet exists yet.

This field shows the employee's timesheet for the current week including its approval status (draft, submitted, approved, or rejected) and total hours logged. If the employee has not created a timesheet for this week, this field is null.

Timesheets in 'draft' status can be modified. 'Submitted' timesheets are pending approval. 'Approved' timesheets are locked and cannot be changed. 'Rejected' timesheets can be edited and resubmitted.
currentTimesheet.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_track_timesheets via LEFT JOIN on authenticated employee.id AND week_start_date = current week Monday. Returns IHrmTimeTrackTimesheet.ISummary if exists, null if no timesheet for current week. Week boundaries: Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59 in organization timezone.

employee.description:
The authenticated employee's record showing identity, position, department, and role within the current organization.

This field provides the employee's core information including their user identity (name, email from member relation), job title, department assignment, role assignment, employment type (full-time, part-time, contractor, intern), and employment status (active, on leave, terminated).

For users belonging to multiple organizations, this shows the employee record for the currently selected organization context.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_track_employees via JOIN on authenticated employee.id from JWT session. Returns IHrmTimeTrackEmployee.ISummary with employee identity, position, department, role, employment type, and status. Organization context from session ensures correct employee record is retrieved for multi-organization users.

projectMemberships.description:
List of active projects the employee is assigned to, including project details and the employee's role on each project.

Each project membership shows the project name, status, color code, and the employee's assigned role (member or project-lead). Only projects with status 'active' are included. Archived or completed projects are excluded.

The list may be empty if the employee is not assigned to any active projects.
projectMemberships.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_track_project_members via JOIN on authenticated employee.id. Filter: deleted_at IS NULL, project.status = 'active'. Returns array of IHrmTimeTrackProjectMember.ISummary objects including project details and assigned role. Empty array if no active project memberships.

recentTimelogs.description:
Time entries logged by the employee during the current week (Monday-Sunday).

Each timelog shows the date, duration, billable status, notes, and associated project and task. Timelogs are ordered by date with most recent first. Only timelogs within the current week boundaries are included.

The list may be empty if the employee has not logged any time entries this week.
recentTimelogs.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_track_timelogs via JOIN on authenticated employee.id. Filter: date >= current week Monday AND date <= current week Sunday, deleted_at IS NULL. Returns array of IHrmTimeTrackTimelog.ISummary objects ordered by date DESC. Empty array if no timelogs in current week.

statistics.description:
Summary statistics providing quick insights into the employee's work activity and timesheet status.

**totalActiveTasks**: The count of open and in-progress tasks assigned to the employee.

**hoursLoggedThisWeek**: The total hours worked during the current week, calculated from all timelog entries. Shown as a decimal number (e.g., 37.5 for 37 hours 30 minutes).

**pendingTimesheets**: The count of timesheets in 'submitted' status awaiting approval. This helps the employee track their submission backlog.

All statistics are calculated in real-time and reflect the current state of the employee's work data.
statistics.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregations from multiple sources:
- totalActiveTasks: COUNT(hrm_time_track_tasks) WHERE employee.id = authenticated.id AND status IN ('open', 'in-progress') AND deleted_at IS NULL
- hoursLoggedThisWeek: SUM(duration_seconds) / 3600 FROM hrm_time_track_timelogs WHERE employee.id = authenticated.id AND date >= current week Monday AND date <= current week Sunday AND deleted_at IS NULL
- pendingTimesheets: COUNT(hrm_time_track_timesheets) WHERE employee.id = authenticated.id AND status = 'submitted' AND deleted_at IS NULL
All values are non-negative. Returns 0 for hoursLoggedThisWeek if no timelogs exist.

IHrmTimeTrackPersonalDashboard.description:
Personal dashboard data for authenticated employees showing work activities, time tracking, and project assignments.

The dashboard consolidates active tasks, recent timelogs, current timesheet status, project memberships, and summary statistics into a single view. All data is scoped to the employee's current organization context.

Dashboard components include:

**Active Tasks**: Open and in-progress tasks assigned to the employee, ordered by due date and priority.

**Recent Timelogs**: Time entries logged during the current week (Monday-Sunday).

**Current Timesheet**: The timesheet for the current week if it exists, including status and total hours.

**Project Memberships**: Active projects the employee is assigned to with their role.

**Statistics**: Summary metrics including total active tasks, hours logged this week, and pending timesheets.
IHrmTimeTrackPersonalDashboard.x-autobe-specification:
Computed dashboard aggregating data from multiple sources for the authenticated employee:

**Source Tables and JOINs**:
1. hrm_time_track_employees - authenticated employee from current organization context (JWT session)
2. hrm_time_track_tasks - JOIN on employee.id, filter status IN ('open', 'in-progress'), order by due_date ASC, priority DESC
3. hrm_time_track_timelogs - JOIN on employee.id, filter date >= current week Monday AND date <= current week Sunday
4. hrm_time_track_timesheets - LEFT JOIN on employee.id AND week_start_date = current week Monday (nullable)
5. hrm_time_track_project_members - JOIN on employee.id, filter project.status = 'active'

**Aggregation Formulas**:
- totalActiveTasks: COUNT of tasks with status IN ('open', 'in-progress') for the employee
- hoursLoggedThisWeek: SUM(duration_seconds) / 3600 for timelogs in current week
- pendingTimesheets: COUNT of timesheets with status = 'submitted' for current employee

**Business Rules**:
- All queries scoped to employee's current organization (from JWT session)
- currentTimesheet is null if no timesheet exists for current week
- Empty arrays returned if no active tasks, timelogs, or project memberships
- Statistics always included even if zero values

**Edge Cases**:
- No timesheet for current week: return null for currentTimesheet
- No active tasks: return empty array for activeTasks
- No timelogs this week: return empty array for recentTimelogs
- No project memberships: return empty array for projectMemberships

id.description:
Unique identifier for the department.

This UUID identifies the department within the organization and is used to reference the department in other system operations.
id.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_track_departments.id. Unique identifier for the department within the organization, retrieved from the department record.

name.description:
Name of the department.

The human-readable name used to identify the department in the organizational structure and user interfaces.
name.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_track_departments.name. The display name of the department retrieved from the department record.

description.description:
Optional description of the department.

Provides additional context about the department's purpose, responsibilities, and scope within the organization. May be null if no description has been provided.
description.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_track_departments.description. Nullable field containing additional information about the department's purpose and scope, retrieved from the department record.

employee_count.description:
Number of active employees assigned to this department.

This count includes only employees with active status (not soft-deleted) who are currently assigned to the department. The value is computed in real-time from the employee records and reflects the current workforce distribution.
employee_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed by COUNT(*) from hrm_time_track_employees where hrm_time_track_department_id matches the department id AND deleted_at IS NULL. Returns integer >= 0 representing the number of active employees assigned to this department.

children.description:
Nested child departments in the organizational hierarchy.

Contains an array of sub-departments that report to this department. Each child department includes its own statistics and may contain further nested children, enabling a complete multi-level organizational tree view. Empty array if this department has no sub-departments.
children.x-autobe-specification: Computed recursive array of IHrmTimeTrackDepartmentReport.IStatistic for all direct child departments. Built by querying hrm_time_track_departments where parent_department_id equals this department's id. Sorted alphabetically by name. Empty array if no child departments exist.

IHrmTimeTrackDepartmentReport.IStatistic.description:
Hierarchical department statistic containing department identification, employee count, and nested child departments for organizational analysis.

This type represents a single department in the organizational hierarchy with its associated employee statistics. Each department includes its unique identifier, name, optional description, and the count of active employees assigned to it. The children array contains nested department statistics for sub-departments, enabling a complete tree view of the organizational structure.

The hierarchical structure allows for multi-level department organization, where top-level departments contain their direct child departments, which in turn may contain their own children, forming a complete organizational tree.
IHrmTimeTrackDepartmentReport.IStatistic.x-autobe-specification:
Compute hierarchical department report from hrm_time_track_departments and hrm_time_track_employees tables.

1. Query hrm_time_track_departments for active departments (deleted_at IS NULL) belonging to the authenticated user's organization.
2. For each department, LEFT JOIN with hrm_time_track_employees and COUNT active employees (deleted_at IS NULL) where hrm_time_track_department_id matches.
3. Build hierarchical tree by joining departments with their parent using parent_department_id.
4. Include: id, name, description (nullable), employee_count (integer >= 0), children (recursive array).
5. Sort departments alphabetically by name within each parent level.
6. Return array of top-level departments (parent_department_id IS NULL) with nested children.

Edge cases: Empty departments have employee_count = 0. Departments with no children have empty children array.

value.description:
Array of permission codes granted to the member through their role assignment.

Each permission code represents a specific capability or access level within the organization. Valid permission codes include organization_management, employee_management, employee_viewing, project_management, project_viewing, time_management, timesheet_approval, time_viewing_all, and report_viewing.

The array may be empty if the member has no employee record in the organization, has no role assigned, or if their role has no permissions configured.
value.x-autobe-specification:
Computed array of permission codes from hrm_time_track_role_permissions table.

Computation logic:
1. Use member_id and organization_id from session to find employee record in hrm_time_track_employees
2. Get role_id from the employee record
3. Query hrm_time_track_role_permissions where role_id matches to get all permission_code values
4. Return array of permission strings

Data source: hrm_time_track_role_permissions.permission_code column, joined via hrm_time_track_employees.role_id and hrm_time_track_roles.id.

Null handling: Returns empty array if employee not found, role not assigned, or employee/role soft-deleted.

IHrmTimeTrackEffectivePermission.description:
Effective permissions granted to the current member through their role assignment within the organization.

This response contains an array of permission codes that determine what actions the member can perform within the organization. Permission codes control access to organization management, employee management, project management, time tracking, timesheet approval, and reporting features.

If the member has no employee record in the organization, has no role assigned, or if the employee or role is soft-deleted, an empty array is returned in the value property.
IHrmTimeTrackEffectivePermission.x-autobe-specification:
Computed response type aggregating permission codes from multiple database tables.

Data source computation:
1. Extract member_id and organization_id from the authenticated member's session token
2. Query hrm_time_track_employees table to find the employee record where member_id matches and organization_id matches
3. If no employee record exists or the record is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null), return empty array
4. If the employee has no role assigned (role_id is null), return empty array
5. Query hrm_time_track_roles table to verify the role exists and is not soft-deleted
6. If the role is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null), return empty array
7. Query hrm_time_track_role_permissions table to retrieve all permission_code values where role_id matches the employee's role_id
8. Return the array of permission codes in the 'value' property

Error conditions:
- No employee record for member in organization → empty array
- Employee has no role assigned → empty array
- Employee or role is soft-deleted → empty array
- Role has no permissions → empty array

role_id.description:
Unique identifier for the role within the organization.

This UUID identifies the specific role definition and is used to reference the role in employee assignments, permission grants, and other role-related operations.
role_id.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_track_roles.id. This is the primary key of the role record, retrieved from the base query on hrm_time_track_roles table where deleted_at IS NULL and filtered by current organization ID.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the role.

Role names are unique within an organization and are used to identify and display roles in the user interface. Examples include 'Administrator', 'Manager', 'Employee', 'Time Keeper'. The name should be descriptive and distinguishable from other roles in the same organization.
name.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_track_roles.name. Human-readable role name retrieved from the base query on hrm_time_track_roles table. Role names are unique within an organization.

is_builtin.description:
Indicates whether this is a built-in system role or a custom user-created role.

Built-in roles (true) are predefined by the system with standard permission sets and cannot be permanently deleted. Custom roles (false) are created by organization administrators and can be fully managed including deletion. This distinction helps prevent accidental removal of essential system roles while allowing flexibility for organization-specific needs.
is_builtin.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_track_roles.is_builtin. Boolean flag retrieved from the base query indicating whether this is a system-defined built-in role (true) or a user-created custom role (false).

description.description:
Detailed description of the role's purpose and intended use.

The description provides context about what the role is for and what permissions it typically grants. This helps administrators understand when to assign this role to employees. Descriptions can include information about the role's scope, typical use cases, and any special considerations. This field is optional and may be null.
description.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_track_roles.description. Optional text field retrieved from the base query providing context about the role's purpose and intended use. Can be null if no description is provided.

employee_count.description:
Number of active employees currently assigned to this role.

This count represents how many employees in the organization have this role assigned to them. It includes only active employees (not soft-deleted) and helps administrators understand the usage and distribution of each role across the organization.
employee_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT of hrm_time_track_employees WHERE hrm_time_track_role_id = role.id AND deleted_at IS NULL. This counts only active (non-deleted) employees assigned to this role within the current organization.

permission_count.description:
Number of permissions granted to this role.

This count represents the total number of distinct permissions assigned to the role. It helps administrators understand the scope of access that each role provides and can be used to identify roles with overly broad or restrictive permission sets.
permission_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT of hrm_time_track_role_permissions WHERE hrm_time_track_role_id = role.id. This counts all permission entries granted to this role in the role_permissions junction table.

IHrmTimeTrackRoleReport.description:
Role report containing aggregated statistics about role distribution, permission assignments, and usage metrics within the organization.

This report provides insights into how roles are structured and utilized within the organization. It includes information about each active role along with counts of employees assigned to that role and the number of permissions granted to it. The report helps administrators understand their permission structure, identify role usage patterns, and audit access control configurations.

Only active roles (not soft-deleted) within the current organization context are included in this report.
IHrmTimeTrackRoleReport.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation from hrm_time_track_roles joined with hrm_time_track_employees and hrm_time_track_role_permissions.

Query Logic:
1. Base query: SELECT from hrm_time_track_roles WHERE hrm_time_track_organization_id = {currentOrgId} AND deleted_at IS NULL
2. For each role, compute employee_count: LEFT JOIN hrm_time_track_employees ON hrm_time_track_role_id = roles.id AND employees.deleted_at IS NULL, then COUNT()
3. For each role, compute permission_count: LEFT JOIN hrm_time_track_role_permissions ON hrm_time_track_role_id = roles.id, then COUNT()
4. Return array of role objects with aggregated counts

Organization-scoped to the authenticated user's current organization context. Only active (non-deleted) roles are included in the report.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the activity log entry.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the activity log record and is used to reference this specific audit entry in queries, updates, and related operations.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.id. Primary key uniquely identifying each activity log entry. Generated as UUID on record creation.

activity_type.description:
Category of the activity being logged.

This field classifies the type of event that occurred in the system. Standard activity types include employee lifecycle events (employee_created, employee_deactivated), contract modifications (contract_created, contract_modified), project lifecycle events (project_created, project_archived), task status changes (task_status_changed), timesheet workflow events (timesheet_submitted, timesheet_approved, timesheet_rejected), and role/department management events (role_assigned, role_created, department_created).
activity_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.activity_type. Categorizes the type of activity being logged. Examples include: employee_created, employee_deactivated, contract_created, project_archived, task_status_changed, timesheet_submitted, timesheet_approved, role_assigned, department_created.

description.description:
Human-readable description of the activity.

This field provides detailed context about what happened, who was involved, and any relevant details for audit purposes. The description complements the activity_type by explaining the specific circumstances of the event.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.description. Human-readable text describing what happened in this activity. Provides context for audit and compliance purposes.

metadata.description:
Structured data containing action-specific details.

This optional field stores key-value pairs or JSON-like data for complex activity details that don't fit standard fields. It allows flexible storage of event-specific information while maintaining the core schema. Examples include before/after state changes, additional context parameters, or extended audit information.
metadata.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.metadata. Optional JSON string containing structured key-value pairs or complex activity details that don't fit standard fields. Null when no additional structured data is needed.

ip_address.description:
IP address of the user who performed the action.

This optional field captures the client IP address for security auditing and geolocation tracking of activity sources. It helps identify the origin of actions and supports fraud detection and access pattern analysis.
ip_address.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.ip_address. Optional IP address of the user who performed the action. Used for security auditing and geolocation tracking. Null when IP information is not available or not captured.

user_agent.description:
Browser or client user agent string of the user who performed the action.

This optional field provides technical context about the client environment used to trigger the activity. It includes browser type, version, and platform information, which helps with compatibility tracking and security analysis.
user_agent.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.user_agent. Optional browser or client user agent string of the user who performed the action. Provides technical context about the client environment. Null when user agent information is not available.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the activity occurred.

This field records the exact time when the activity took place. It is used for chronological ordering of audit logs, filtering activities by time range, and generating time-based reports. The timestamp is stored in UTC timezone.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.created_at. Timestamp when the activity occurred. This is the actual time of the event, not when the record was inserted. Used for chronological ordering and time-range queries.

organization.description:
Organization that owns this activity log entry.

This required relation establishes the organizational context for the activity log. All activity logs are scoped to a specific organization for multi-tenancy isolation. Users can only view activity logs from organizations they belong to.
organization.x-autobe-specification: Relation from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.organization via JOIN on hrm_time_track_organization_id. Returns IHrmTimeTrackOrganization.ISummary. Required relation - every activity log belongs to exactly one organization for multi-tenancy isolation.

member.description:
User who performed the action recorded in this activity log.

This required relation establishes accountability by tracking which authenticated user triggered the event. The member represents the global user identity across all organizations.
member.x-autobe-specification: Relation from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.member via JOIN on hrm_time_track_member_id. Returns IHrmTimeTrackMember.ISummary. Required relation - every activity log must have an authenticated member who performed the action.

employee.description:
Employee entity affected by this activity, if applicable.

This optional relation is used for employee lifecycle events such as creation, deactivation, department changes, or role assignments. Null when the activity does not involve a specific employee.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Relation from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.employee via LEFT JOIN on hrm_time_track_employee_id. Returns IHrmTimeTrackEmployee.ISummary or null. Optional relation used for employee lifecycle events such as creation, deactivation, department changes, or role assignments.

project.description:
Project entity affected by this activity, if applicable.

This optional relation is used for project lifecycle events such as creation, status changes, or archival. Null when the activity does not involve a specific project.
project.x-autobe-specification: Relation from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.project via LEFT JOIN on hrm_time_track_project_id. Returns IHrmTimeTrackProject.ISummary or null. Optional relation used for project lifecycle events such as creation, status changes, or archival.

task.description:
Task entity affected by this activity, if applicable.

This optional relation is used for task status changes, assignment modifications, or due date updates. Null when the activity does not involve a specific task.
task.x-autobe-specification: Relation from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.task via LEFT JOIN on hrm_time_track_task_id. Returns IHrmTimeTrackTask.ISummary or null. Optional relation used for task status changes, assignment modifications, or due date updates.

timesheet.description:
Timesheet entity affected by this activity, if applicable.

This optional relation is used for timesheet submission, approval, or rejection events. Null when the activity does not involve a specific timesheet.
timesheet.x-autobe-specification: Relation from hrm_time_track_activity_logs.timesheet via LEFT JOIN on hrm_time_track_timesheet_id. Returns IHrmTimeTrackTimesheet.ISummary or null. Optional relation used for timesheet submission, approval, or rejection events.

role.description:
Role entity affected by this activity, if applicable.

This optional relation is used for role creation, modification, or deletion events. Null when the activity does not involve a specific role.

Restricts results to invitations with a specific status. Valid status values are: 'pending' for active invitations awaiting guest acceptance, 'accepted' for invitations that have been consumed when the guest created an account, and 'expired' for invitations that have passed their expiration date. Leave empty to retrieve invitations of all statuses.
status.x-autobe-specification: Filter guest invitations by invitation status. Exact match on the status column: WHERE status = '{status}'. Valid values: 'pending' (awaiting acceptance), 'accepted' (consumed during account creation), 'expired' (past expiration date). Empty or null value means no status filter is applied.

created_after.description:
Filter invitations created after this timestamp.

Restricts results to guest invitations that were created after the specified date and time. Use ISO 8601 datetime format (e.g., '2024-01-15T00:00:00Z'). created_after.x-autobe-specification: Filter guest invitations created after the specified timestamp. Applied as greater-than comparison on created_at column: WHERE created_at > '{created_after}'. ISO 8601 datetime format required (e.g., '2024-01-15T00:00:00Z'). Empty or null value means no lower bound filter is applied.

created_before.description:
Filter invitations created before this timestamp.

Restricts results to guest invitations that were created before the specified date and time. Use ISO 8601 datetime format (e.g., '2024-01-15T23:59:59Z'). This is useful for retrieving invitations up to a specific point in time. Combine with created_after for a date range filter.
created_before.x-autobe-specification: Filter guest invitations created before the specified timestamp. Applied as less-than comparison on created_at column: WHERE created_at < '{created_before}'. ISO 8601 datetime format required (e.g., '2024-01-15T23:59:59Z'). Empty or null value means no upper bound filter is applied.

January = 1, February = 2, ..., December = 12. Used for financial reporting, pay period calculations, and timesheet approval cycles aligned with fiscal periods.
fiscal_start_month.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_organizations.fiscal_start_month. Integer 1-12 representing month number.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the organization was created. Immutable after creation.

This field records when the organization was first established in the system and is used for sorting, filtering, and audit purposes.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_organizations.created_at. DateTime field with timestamptz database type.

IHrmTimeTrackOrganization.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an organization for list displays and reference contexts.

This type provides essential organization information including identification (id, name), optional description, and operational settings (currency, timezone, fiscal start month). The created_at timestamp indicates when the organization was established.

Used in paginated list responses, relation references, and contexts where full organization details are not needed. Provides a lightweight representation optimized for browsing organizations and displaying organizational context in related entity summaries.
IHrmTimeTrackOrganization.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_organizations table. Fields: id, name, description, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month, created_at. Excluded: logo (large URL field not essential for lists), updated_at and deleted_at (internal audit fields). Description is nullable in database, exposed as nullable in DTO using oneOf with null. Filter by organization_id from session context for multi-tenant isolation. Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL) in queries.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the member account.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the member record and is used globally across the system to reference the authenticated user identity. Each member account receives a unique identifier upon creation that remains constant throughout the account lifecycle.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_members.id. Primary key UUID.

email.description:
Unique email address used for authentication and account identification.

This field serves as the primary identifier for login and must be unique across all members. The email address is case-sensitive and stored in lowercase for consistency. Used for account recovery, notifications, and user identification in administrative interfaces.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_members.email. Unique constraint enforced at database level.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the member account was first created.

This immutable timestamp records when the account was initially registered in the system. Used for account age calculations, audit trail purposes, and filtering members by registration date. Format follows ISO 8601 date-time standard with timezone information.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_members.created_at. Immutable timestamp set on account creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the member account was last updated.

This field is automatically updated on any modification to account settings or security credentials. Used to track account changes, detect stale data, and sort members by recent activity. Format follows ISO 8601 date-time standard with timezone information.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_members.updated_at. Automatically updated on any account modification.

IHrmTimeTrackMember.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a member account for list displays and relationship references.

This lightweight DTO provides essential member identity information including unique identifier, email address, and account timestamps. It is used extensively across the system as a reference object in employee records, sessions, verifications, password resets, task histories, timesheet snapshots, activity logs, and timer snapshots.

The summary format optimizes for list views and relationship displays by excluding sensitive data (password hashes), soft-delete timestamps, and composition relationships that are accessed through separate API endpoints.
IHrmTimeTrackMember.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_members table for scalar fields: id, email, created_at, updated_at. Excluded: password_hash (security field, never exposed), deleted_at (soft-delete timestamp not needed in summary). Has-many relations (sessions, passwordResets, emailVerifications, employees, employeeSnapshots, roleSnapshots, approvedTimesheets, timesheetSnapshots, timerSnapshots, activityLogs, taskHistoryEntries) are composition relationships accessed via separate endpoints, not included in ISummary. This summary type is used as a reference object in BELONGS-TO relationships across multiple entities.

functions.content:
import { IEntity } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IEntity";
import { IHrmTimeTrackEmployeeContract } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IHrmTimeTrackEmployeeContract";
import { DeepPartial } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/typings/DeepPartial";
import { ArrayUtil, RandomGenerator } from "@nestia/e2e";
import { randint } from "tstl";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Prepare random HRM time track employee contract creation data for E2E testing.
 *
 * Generates a complete IHrmTimeTrackEmployeeContract.ICreate with randomized values
 * including start date, optional end date, pay rate, pay period frequency, weekly
 * working hours, and optional notes.
 *
 * The contract represents employment terms for an employee including compensation
 * details and working hour expectations. When a new contract is created, any
 * existing active contract for the employee is automatically ended.
 */
export function prepare_random_hrm_time_track_employee_contract(
  input?: DeepPartial<IHrmTimeTrackEmployeeContract.ICreate> | undefined,
): IHrmTimeTrackEmployeeContract.ICreate {
  return {
    start_date:
      input?.start_date ?? typia.random<string & tags.Format<"date-time">>(),
    end_date:
      input?.end_date ??
      (Math.random() > 0.3
        ? typia.random<string & tags.Format<"date-time">>()
        : null),
    pay_rate:
      input?.pay_rate ??
      typia.random<
        number & tags.Type<"uint32"> & tags.Minimum<1000> & tags.Maximum<100000>
      >(),
    pay_period:
      input?.pay_period ??
      RandomGenerator.pick(["weekly", "biweekly", "monthly"] as const),
    working_hours_per_week:
      input?.working_hours_per_week ??
      typia.random<
        number & tags.Type<"uint32"> & tags.Minimum<20> & tags.Maximum<60>
      >(),
    notes:
      input?.notes ??
      (Math.random() > 0.5
        ? RandomGenerator.paragraph({ sentences: 3 })
        : null),
  };
}

scenario.draft:
Test the primary success path for guest invitation acceptance.

1. Prepare test data: A pending guest invitation record with valid email, invitation token, organization, and role
2. Call the guest join endpoint with:
   - email: matching the pending invitation
   - invitationToken: valid token from the invitation
   - password: new password for the account
   - name: display name for the user profile
   - href: current page URL
   - referrer: referring page URL
   - ip: optional client IP address
3. Verify the response contains:
   - IHrmTimeTrackGuest.IAuthorized structure with guest identity
   - JWT access token and refresh token in the token object
   - Organization and role summary information
   - Status updated to 'accepted'
4. Verify database state:
   - New member record created in hrm_time_track_members
   - New user profile created in hrm_time_track_user_profiles
   - New employee record created linking user to organization with assigned role
   - Guest invitation status updated to 'accepted'
   - Guest session record created in hrm_time_track_guest_sessions
5. Verify the invitation cannot be reused (second join attempt should fail)

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /hrmTimeTrack/auth/guest/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'guest' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

scenario.draft:
Test the business rule that expired invitations cannot be accepted.

1. Prepare test data: A guest invitation record with:
   - Valid email and invitation token
   - Status set to 'pending'
   - expires_at timestamp in the past (expired)
   - Associated organization and role
2. Call the guest join endpoint with:
   - email: matching the expired invitation
   - invitationToken: valid token from the expired invitation
   - password: new password for the account
   - name: display name for the user profile
   - href: current page URL
   - referrer: referring page URL
3. Verify the response returns HTTP 400 status code
4. Verify the error indicates the invitation has expired
5. Verify no user account was created (no member record in database)
6. Verify no user profile was created
7. Verify no employee record was created
8. Verify the guest invitation status remains 'pending' (not changed to 'accepted')
9. Verify no guest session was created

This test validates the business rule that invitations must be accepted before their expiration date to prevent stale invitations from being used.

scenario.draft:
Test the primary success path for guest session token refresh.

1. First, accept a guest invitation by calling /hrmTimeTrack/auth/guest/join with valid invitation email and token. This creates the guest account, employee record, and initial session.
2. Extract the refresh token from the join response.
3. Call /hrmTimeTrack/auth/guest/refresh with the refresh token in the request body.
4. Verify the response returns IHrmTimeTrackGuest.IAuthorized with new access token, refresh token, and updated expiration timestamps.
5. Verify the new expired_at timestamp is extended from the original session.
6. Verify the guest identity (id, email, status) is included in the response.
7. Verify the organization and role information are nested in the response.
8. Confirm the guest can use the new access token for subsequent authenticated requests.

This validates the core business workflow where guests maintain authenticated access during the invitation acceptance process without interruption.

scenario.draft:
Test the edge case where a guest attempts to refresh tokens but the linked invitation has expired.

1. First, accept a guest invitation by calling /hrmTimeTrack/auth/guest/join with valid invitation email and token. This creates the guest account and initial session.
2. Extract the refresh token from the join response.
3. Simulate invitation expiration (via database or test setup) - set the guest invitation's expires_at to a past timestamp or change status to 'expired'.
4. Call /hrmTimeTrack/auth/guest/refresh with the refresh token.
5. Verify the system returns HTTP 400 Bad Request because the linked invitation is no longer valid.
6. Verify the error response indicates the invitation has expired or is not in a valid state.
7. Confirm the guest session is not extended and no new tokens are issued.

This validates the business rule that guest session refresh requires a valid, non-expired invitation. The system must reject refresh attempts when the underlying invitation is no longer active.

scenario.draft:
Test successful member login with valid credentials.

**Setup**:
1. First register a new member account using the join endpoint with a valid email and password
2. Note the email and password used for registration

**Execution**:
1. Call the login endpoint with the registered email and password
2. Include required session context fields: href, referrer, and optionally ip

**Validation**:
1. Verify HTTP 200 OK response
2. Verify response contains member identity (id, email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at)
3. Verify deleted_at is null (account is active)
4. Verify response contains authorization token with access, refresh, expired_at, and refreshable_until fields
5. Verify the access token is a valid JWT string
6. Verify the refresh token is a valid JWT string
7. Verify expired_at and refreshable_until are valid ISO 8601 timestamps
8. Verify the returned member id matches the registered member

**Business Rules**:
- Login succeeds only when email exists and password matches
- New session is created in hrm_time_track_member_sessions
- JWT tokens are generated with appropriate expiration times

**Execution**:

2. Include required session context fields: href, referrer

**Validation**:
1. Verify HTTP 401 Unauthorized response
2. Verify no authorization tokens are returned
3. Verify no member identity information is leaked in the response
4. Verify the system does not reveal whether the email exists or the password is incorrect (security requirement)

**Business Rules**:
- Login is rejected when password does not match the stored hash
- System maintains security by not disclosing specific failure reason
- No session is created for failed login attempts

**Alternative Test**:

scenario.draft:
Test the filtering functionality of the member list endpoint with email and status filters.

**Setup:**
- Ensure member accounts exist with various email addresses and statuses (active and deleted)

**Test Steps:**
1. Test email partial match filter:
   - Call PATCH /hrmTimeTrack/members with email filter (e.g., 'john@example')
   - Verify only members with email addresses containing the filter string are returned
   - Verify the matching is case-insensitive

2. Test status filter for active members:
   - Call PATCH /hrmTimeTrack/members with status='active'
   - Verify only members with deleted_at=NULL are returned
   - Verify soft-deleted members are excluded from results

3. Test status filter for deleted members:
   - Call PATCH /hrmTimeTrack/members with status='deleted'
   - Verify only soft-deleted members (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are returned
   - Verify active members are excluded from results

4. Test combined filters:
   - Call PATCH /hrmTimeTrack/members with both email and status filters
   - Verify results match both filter criteria simultaneously

5. Test date range filters:
   - Call PATCH /hrmTimeTrack/members with created_at_gte and created_at_lte parameters
   - Verify only members created within the specified date range are returned

**Validation Points:**
- Email filter uses case-insensitive partial matching (ILIKE behavior)
- Status filter correctly distinguishes between active (deleted_at=NULL) and deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) members
- Date range filters use >= and <= operators correctly
- Combined filters work together as expected (AND logic)
- Empty results are returned gracefully when no members match the filter criteria
- Pagination continues to work correctly with filters applied

- Response status is 200 OK
- Snapshot id matches the requested snapshotId
- Snapshot timerId matches the requested timerId

- started_at contains valid ISO 8601 datetime

- project relation contains IHrmTimeTrackProject.ISummary with the associated project
- task relation contains IHrmTimeTrackTask.ISummary or null (if timer had no task)
- member relation contains IHrmTimeTrackMember.ISummary with the member who triggered the event

**Business Logic Validation**:
- Verify the snapshot data is denormalized and immutable (audit trail integrity)
- Verify all relationship data is included even if parent records are modified later
- Verify organization-level data isolation (member can only access snapshots from their organization)

scenario.draft:
Test retrieving a hierarchical department report with employee statistics for an organization that has multiple departments with nested child departments and employees assigned.

**Setup**:
1. Register and authenticate as a member
2. Create an organization
3. Create multiple departments with parent-child relationships (e.g., Engineering with sub-departments Backend, Frontend, QA)
4. Create employees and assign them to various departments

**Test Steps**:
1. Call GET /hrmTimeTrack/member/reports/departments
2. Verify response returns an array of top-level departments
3. Verify each department contains: id, name, description (nullable), employee_count (integer >= 0), children (array)
4. Verify hierarchical structure: child departments are nested under their parent departments
5. Verify employee_count accurately reflects the number of active employees assigned to each department
6. Verify departments are sorted alphabetically by name within each parent level
7. Verify only active departments (not soft-deleted) are included
8. Verify only active employees (not soft-deleted) are counted

**Expected Result**:
- HTTP 200 OK
- Response body contains hierarchical department structure with accurate employee counts
- Departments with no children have empty children array
- Departments with no employees have employee_count = 0

scenario.draft:
Test retrieving a department report when some departments have been soft-deleted.

**Setup**:
1. Register and authenticate as a member
2. Create an organization
3. Create multiple departments (e.g., Engineering, Sales, Marketing)
4. Create employees and assign them to departments
5. Soft-delete one of the departments (e.g., Marketing)

**Test Steps**:
1. Call GET /hrmTimeTrack/member/reports/departments
2. Verify response includes only active (non-deleted) departments
3. Verify the deleted department (Marketing) is NOT included in the response
4. Verify employee counts for remaining departments are accurate
5. Verify employees that were assigned to the deleted department now have null department assignment (per section 234)

**Expected Result**:
- HTTP 200 OK
- Response body contains only active departments (Engineering, Sales)
- Deleted department (Marketing) is excluded from the report
- Employee counts reflect only employees assigned to active departments

**Business Rule Validation**:
- According to section 236, when a department is deleted, it SHALL be removed from the department list

Collects organization creation data to hrm_time_track_organizations table. All required fields (name, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month) and optional fields (description, logo) are in the request body. No external references needed as organization is a root entity with no foreign keys.
Collects IHrmTimeTrackDepartment.ICreate to hrm_time_track_departments. Organization FK comes from session context, not request body.
Collects IHrmTimeTrackProject.ICreate to hrm_time_track_projects. Organization reference comes from authenticated session context.

Collects IHrmTimeTrackTask.ICreate to hrm_time_track_tasks. All FK references (project, employee, parent task) are in the request body, no external references needed.
